$comment: Performance budgets for the top 20 endpoints. p95 in ms, error rate is the max fraction of non-2xx/3xx responses tolerated. schemaVersion 2 re-baselines the original dev-seeded values to the production-shaped steady state described in docs/ops/capacity.md §1 (LOAD_PROFILE=nightly, 50 VUs, 10 min, 3 seeded tenants, prod build) — the shape the nightly k6 run in .github/workflows/load-test-nightly.yml lands at. Per-endpoint p95 values are rounded up with ~10–15% headroom (cheap auth/preference reads to the next 20 ms, list/aggregate reads to the next 50 ms); error budgets stay at the dev seed since the nightly run consistently came in at <0.1% non-2xx. Until the rolling re-baseline automation in follow-up #2542 lands, treat these as the budget-bar derived from the documented ceiling rather than direct artifact aggregates. The CI checker (loadtests/check-budgets.mjs) fails when p95 exceeds budget by more than `regressionTolerance` percent or when error rate exceeds budget. See docs/ops/capacity.md §1 for the tested ceiling and §5 for the re-baselining procedure.
$mutationsComment: Per-endpoint budgets for the write/mutation workload exercised by loadtests/scenarios/mutations.js (nightly). p95 budgets are sized for the same `LOAD_PROFILE=nightly` shape as the read budgets above but allow the extra DB round-trip(s) and the audit-log + RLS overhead each tenant write incurs (see docs/architecture/tenant-isolation.md). Insert paths get the most headroom because they touch the most tables (audit_log + entity row + frequently a join table); status-only PATCHes are tighter. Error rate stays at 1% — the same tolerance the global ceiling uses — because mutation 4xxs are dominated by validation responses, which are still healthy 200s from a server-perspective. The CI checker enforces these alongside the `endpoints` block.
